THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, MARCH 21, 1936.

SHAREHOLDERS PROTECTION
ASSOCIATION MOBILIZES AND
APPOINTS NOMINEE TO BOARD

The 21st annual general meeting of the shareholders of the Shanghai Seremban Rubber Estates, Limited, was held at No. 93 Canton Road, at 4 p.m. yesterday. Mr. A. J. Welch (Chairman of the Board) presided and was supported by Messrs. L. E. Canning, H. Kadoorie and M. Spelman (Directors), Reader Harris (Legal adviser), and C. F. Shackleton (Secretary).

The total number of shares represented was 242,800. There were 19 shareholders present, including several leading members of the newly-formed Shanghai Shareholders Protection Association. The meeting lasted an hour and a half and many interesting points were raised.

Chairman's Speech
Addressing the meeting the Chairman said:
Gentlemen; The report and accounts having been in your hands for the requisite period, I propose with your permission, to follow the usual procedure and to take them as read.

The result of the year's working has been a profit of Shanghai $17,944.34 as compared with a profit for the previous year of Shanghai $39,303.88. The decrease is mainly attributable to the fact that owing to the operation of the scheme for the restriction of output the amount of rubber produced was 45,130 lbs. smaller than it was during the previous year, whilst the net price realized was only a trifle higher per pound. Furthermore, the Estate expenditure was St. $6,629.92 greater. The main items which contributed to this increase were general charges which were St. $1,154 higher owing to an additional sum of St. $980, having been spent on the upkeep of buildings, and St. $305 on recruiting due to an increase in the rate of Tamil assessment, most other items under this heading showed a decrease.

Rent was higher by St. $716 due to the Rebate granted by Government being rescinded. The cost of the upkeep of the producing area was St. $1,046 greater owing to higher wages and the necessity of removing the bracken and other rough growths from the gardens. In spite of the smaller crop the cost of tapping and manufacture was up by St. $1,781 due to the higher wages that had to be paid and duty was greater by St. $1,964 owing to the incidence of a Government cess of 7/10ths of a cent per pound on the amount of rubber exportable.

The Shanghai office expenses showed a small increase on account of printing, postage and advertisements with regard to the dividend paid in March 1935. The financial position of the Company is very strong and at December 31, 1935, the net surplus assets amounted to $101,449.00, while the dividend recommended by the Board will only absorb $16,260.

Estate Matters
Turning to Estate matters, there is as usual very little to say. The Estate has continued to be maintained in good order and condition. A prominent Chinese shareholder to join the Board.

In conclusion, Gentlemen, I would like to express best thanks to the Manager, to the Visiting Agents and to the Agents in the Straits for the efficient manner in which they have administered the affairs of the Estate.

I will now formally propose that the annual report and statement of accounts as presented be adopted and passed. This is seconded by Mr. H. Kadoorie and the matter is now open for discussion.

Mr. Gubbay's Queries
Mr. Gubbay said he should like to know if anyone present considered the expenditure of $5,743 for Shanghai office expenses reasonable. The acreage of this Estate was 638 acres and therefore this worked out at $9 per planted acre. He supposed he should be told that this charge included office rent, telephone and sundry other charges—but even then he submitted the charge was excessive for the work done. How many working days per month did the secretaryship of a company of that size involve? Surely not more than three full working days per month in the ordinary way of business and perhaps twice that number of working days when the accounts were prepared for the annual audit. He said the Company was paying too much. If the secretaries did not see their way to reducing the charges, then he said it was the duty of, and business of, the Directors to see that competitive terms were obtained to enable such reductions to take place. The work at this end was not so highly specialized but that it would be impossible to obtain other firms to take up the work, seeing that chartered accountants had been constantly employed to audit and settle the form of accounts every year. But one way to effect this reduction of expenses amicably would be to formulate a scheme for the amalgamation of all the Rubber Companies here into one. If he might suggest it, in a friendly way, amalgamation might be considered from the point of view of the valuation of Estates per acre, rather than per share, in order to absorb the 'lamer ducks' more early, and from the point of view of local management, one local board, one office, and one set of secretaries would suffice. There were other points in the accounts which called for attention. The item—bonus and commission—required elucidation. To whom and for what was this sum of $1,645 paid? General charges at $6,977 were $1,052 higher than last year, in a year when profits and dividends were lower. The shareholders got less, but the expenses increased.

Cheaper Service in Malaya?
Mr. Hickling seconded the remarks of Mr. Gubbay. He made a special point of the fact that he believed it was possible to get cheaper service at the moment and to-day. He strongly supported the idea of amalgamation although he thought...

Mr. D. C. Raphael.
Mr. Pennell New Director
The next resolution on the agenda was that Mr. L. E. Canning be re-elected a Director of the Company, proposed by Mr. E. F. Parsons, seconded by Mr. O. Dierckx.

Mr. Hickling proposed and Mr. Soyka seconded an amendment that Mr. W. A. Pennell be elected a Director in Mr. Canning's place.

Mr. Gensburger said Mr. Hickling had just spoken about economies and now he wanted to put up a new Director in Mr. Canning's stead. Personally he thought if Mr. Canning were outvoted there should be no Director put in his stead, then Mr. Hickling would be consistent.

Mr. Hickling explained his seeming inconsistency by saying that he proposed to make it a recommendation to the incoming Board that the Directors' fees should not exceed $1,500 to be divided among them.

Mr. Pennell, in explaining his stand, said he thought it was fundamentally unsound and ethically wrong for a gentleman connected with the management of Rubber Companies to be on the Board of Directors.

The Chairman said this was the universal practice both here and at home. In a sense it was a protection for the other Directors because Directors were liable to all sorts of pains and penalties and if the General Manager was also a Director he was liable to the same pains and penalties as the other Directors.

The amendment was carried by nine votes to eight and Mr. Pennell was declared duly elected a Director of the Company.

After some discussion, the resolution that Messrs. Thomson and Co. be re-elected auditors, proposed by Mr. Chas. A. Howard, and seconded by Mr. M. E. Dangoor was carried unanimously.

Action Through Rubber Trust
Mr. Gensburger pointed out the difficulties of amalgamation in the ordinary way and said that such procedure could be blocked by a comparatively small shareholder standing out. But there was a practical way, he believed, and that was through the Rubber Trust. The Rubber Trust Company was formed originally with a very large capital, the idea being to gradually absorb the other Rubber Companies. Now here was the idea he would like to put before the Directors at that meeting and also Mr. Hickling. He thought they should get a fair, independent valuation of their Malayan property and then approach the Rubber Trust with the possible result that eventually the Rubber Trust would offer any one of their shares in exchange for, say, three or four Serembans according to ratio shown by the valuations. The result would be that in a short while the Rubber Trust would control most of their shares and Serembans might go quietly into liquidation. If this method of absorbing the Rubber Companies were adopted, he pointed out, they would come to have unified control and a great saving of expense.

《字林西报》，1936年3月21日，星期六。

股东保护协会动员并任命董事候选人

上海森美兰橡胶种植园有限公司（Shanghai Seremban Rubber Estates, Limited）第二十一届股东周年大会于昨日下午4时在广东路93号举行。董事会主席A. J. Welch先生主持会议，出席者包括L. E. Canning、H. Kadoorie和M. Spelman先生（董事）、Reader Harris（法律顾问）以及C. F. Shackleton（秘书）。

代表股份总数为242,800股。出席会议的股东共19人，其中包括新成立的上海股东保护协会的几位主要成员。会议持续了一个半小时，会上提出了许多值得关注的议题。

主席致辞
主席在向大会致辞时说：
诸位先生；鉴于报告及账目已按法定期限送达各位手中，我提议在征得各位同意后，遵循惯例，视报告及账目已宣读完毕。

本年度经营结果为盈利上海银17,944.34两，而上一年度盈利为上海银39,303.88两。利润减少主要归因于限产计划的实施，导致橡胶产量较上一年度减少了45,130磅，而每磅实现的净价仅略高一点。此外，种植园支出增加了圣洋银6,629.92两。造成这一增加的主要项目是一般费用，由于额外支出了圣洋银980两用于建筑物维护，以及因泰米尔人（Tamil）人头税税率提高而多支出圣洋银305两用于招募工人，该类别下的其他大多数项目均有所减少。

租金增加了圣洋银716两，原因是政府取消了一项退税优惠。生产区的维护成本增加了圣洋银1,046两，原因是工资上涨以及必须清除花园中的蕨类植物和其他杂草。尽管收成减少，但由于必须支付更高的工资，割胶和加工成本仍增加了圣洋银1,781两；此外，由于政府对可出口橡胶数量征收每磅7/10仙的附加税，关税增加了圣洋银1,964两。

上海办事处费用因印刷、邮资以及关于1935年3月派发股息的公告广告费而略有增加。公司财务状况非常强劲，截至1935年12月31日，净资产盈余达101,449.00美元，而董事会建议派发的股息仅需动用16,260美元。

种植园事务
谈到种植园事务，照例没有什么可多说的。种植园一直保持良好的秩序和状态。一位重要的中国股东将加入董事会。

最后，诸位先生，我要向经理、巡视代理以及海峡殖民地代理表示最诚挚的谢意，感谢他们高效地管理了种植园的事务。

我现在正式提议通过并提交所呈报的年度报告和财务报表。此动议由H. Kadoorie先生附议，现在开放讨论。

Gubbay先生的质询
Gubbay先生说，他想知道在座是否有人认为上海办事处费用5,743美元是合理的。该种植园面积为638英亩，因此折合每英亩种植面积费用为9美元。他猜想有人会告诉他，这笔费用包括办公室租金、电话费及其他杂费——但即便如此，他认为相对于所做的工作而言，这笔费用过高。像这样规模的公司，其秘书工作每月涉及多少个工作日？按常规业务计算，每月肯定不超过三个全天工作日，而在准备年度审计账目时，或许也就是这个数字的两倍。他说公司支付的费用太多了。如果秘书们无法找到降低费用的途径，那么董事会有责任也有义务去寻求具有竞争力的条款，以实现此类削减。这方面的工作并非高度专业化，以至于不可能找到其他公司来承接这项工作，毕竟每年都聘请特许会计师来审计并确定账目格式。不过，要友好地实现这种费用削减，一个办法是制定方案，将此处所有的橡胶公司合并为一。如果允许他以友好的方式提出建议，可以从每英亩种植园估值而非每股估值的角度来考虑合并，以便更早地吸收那些“病弱企业”（lame ducks），并且从本地管理的角度来看，一个本地董事会、一个办事处和一套秘书班子就足够了。账目中还有其他几点也值得关注。“奖金和佣金”一项需要澄清。这笔1,645美元的款项支付给了谁？为何支付？一般费用为6,977美元，比去年高出1,052美元，而这一年利润和股息都较低。股东所得减少，但费用却增加了。

马来亚的服务更便宜？
Hickling先生附议了Gubbay先生的发言。他特别指出，他认为目前和今天都有可能获得更廉价的服务。他强烈支持合并的想法，尽管他认为……

D. C. Raphael先生。
Pennell先生为新任董事
议程上的下一项决议是重新选举L. E. Canning先生为公司董事，由E. F. Parsons先生提议，O. Dierckx先生附议。

Hickling先生提议，并由Soyka先生附议一项修正案，选举W. A. Pennell先生接替Canning先生担任董事。

Gensburger先生说，Hickling先生刚才还在谈论节约开支，现在却想推举一位新董事取代Canning先生。就个人而言，他认为如果Canning先生在投票中落选，就不应再推举任何人取代他的位置，这样Hickling先生才能做到前后一致。

Hickling先生解释了他看似不一致的地方，他说他打算向新一届董事会建议，董事酬金总额不应超过1,500美元，由各位董事分配。

Pennell先生在解释自己的立场时说，他认为让一位与橡胶公司管理层有关联的人士进入董事会，从根本上说是站不住脚的，且在道德上是错误的。

主席说，无论在此地还是在本国，这都是普遍做法。从某种意义上说，这也是对其他董事的一种保护，因为董事需承担各种痛苦和处罚，如果总经理也是董事，他将与其他董事承担同样的痛苦和处罚。

修正案以九票对八票获得通过，Pennell先生被宣布正式当选为公司董事。

经过一番讨论，由Chas. A. Howard先生提议、M. E. Dangoor先生附议的重新选举Thomson & Co.为审计师的决议获得一致通过。

通过橡胶托拉斯采取行动
Gensburger先生指出了以常规方式进行合并的困难，并表示，只要有相对较小的股东反对，这种程序就可能受阻。但他相信有一个切实可行的办法，那就是通过橡胶托拉斯。橡胶托拉斯公司最初成立时资本非常雄厚，其构想是逐步吸收其他橡胶公司。现在，他想在本次会议上向董事们以及Hickling先生提出这个想法。他认为，他们应该对其马来亚财产进行公正、独立的估值，然后接触橡胶托拉斯，可能的结果是，最终橡胶托拉斯会根据估值显示的比例，用其股份交换，比如说，三到四股森美兰公司的股票。结果将是，在短时间内，橡胶托拉斯将控制他们的大部分股份，而森美兰公司可能会悄然进入清算程序。他指出，如果采用这种吸收橡胶公司的方法，他们将实现统一控制并大幅节省费用。

主席承诺将对提出的各种建议……

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, MARCH 18, 1936

Shareholders' Protection
Group's First Meeting

Mr. N. W. Hickling Takes Chair, Executive Board
Is Elected; Criticism By Member Who Wants
Referendum Of Rubber Company Investors

The Shanghai Shareholders Protection Association held its inaugural meeting yesterday afternoon in the Royal Asiatic Society Hall with a gathering of 44 persons present, 22 of whom were voting as members of the new organization in the election of an Executive Committee.

Mr. N. W. Hickling, having been voted to the chair, asked Mr. F. L. Morrison and Mr. L. Fearon to support him as legal adviser and secretary, respectively.

Mr. Hickling said:—To start with, this meeting is entirely informal and called for the purpose of avoiding being called "embryonic" in the future.

Before getting down to the actual business such as the formation of this association and appointing an executive committee, I wish to say a few words, not only on the aims and objects of the association, but how we suggest to run it. In the first place, we have got to cut our coat according to our cloth; in other words, the work we can attempt must be to a great extent governed by the funds we have in the bank and the amount of hard work done free by members themselves.

That we run on business lines is absolutely essential and these lines will have to be on the co-operative club idea, and certainly not with the idea that once you have paid your annual subscription that your responsibility, for you have no liability, has been done. The amount of work that Mr. Fearon and myself, Mr. Pennell and Mr. Mathews, have done in forming this association, is far greater than any of you realize.

No Regular Salary

Mr. Fearon has received a pittance for his work. He has no fixed salary and has only drawn trifles when necessary. Mr. Fearon will continue to act as Secretary, and the idea is that your committee, when appointed, will form sub-committees, on which members will be invited to serve and be expected to serve. That is why I have used the word co-operative. These sub-committees will make their reports to the Executive Committee who will take action if necessary, and I honestly believe if we work on these lines, we can attain the objects of the association and become a useful and respected body in Shanghai.

At present we are under suspicion and possibly not unreasonably. We have got to prove that although we may break some eggs in the process we always have the omelette in view and that we have got a reasonable knowledge of cooking.

Resolutions were then passed to form the association to be known as the Shanghai Shareholders' Protection Association, and to take the Memorandum and Articles of Association of the London Shareholders' Protection Association as a basis, subject to such modifications as necessary.

Election Contest

A contest ensued in the choice of 10 members for the executive committee when Dr. O. Fisher was nominated from the floor. Ballots were given to members who were asked to write the name of the man they wished eliminated, and signed so that non-members could not vote. The result was that Dr. Fisher was eliminated and the following were elected: Captain W. ... T. ... C. ... Dr. ... L. ...

Mr. Hickling then said he did not propose to discuss himself the aims and objects of the association, since the meeting was called to do the work that had now been done. He merely proposed to ask anyone who had suggestions...

At first there was nobody who put forth questions or suggestions, and Mr. Hickling said that he would ask the non-members who would like to join to leave their names with Mr. Fearon. He said he hoped further meetings would be called and that he would have good results to report.

As the meeting was about to break up, Mr. Brian Bates said:

Referendum Scheme

When this association was first mooted, I immediately sent around a cheque, but I don't altogether like the lines on which this association is developing. My idea, particularly with reference to the rubber companies, is that it should be run on amalgamation lines, and it seems to me that before anything is done to Messrs. Burkill's and Watties' Ltd., a referendum should be taken of the rubber company shareholders to see if such support is forthcoming. And when you have the support behind you, then instead of requesting them to do this and that you will be able to "tell" them to do it. It seems to me that before we go any further, instead of pin-pricking at these two firms, a referendum should be taken, and unless you get sufficient support it shows the shareholders haven't got sufficient interest. — (Hear, Hear).

In reply, Mr. Hickling said that due reference would be taken by the incoming committee of Mr. Bates' remarks.

He continued:—I do not wish to tell you that we work only by force, that we get proxies and shareholders behind us and force things through. There are many suggestions which have been put forward to your committee to try and get this work done. Your committee is attempting to do this by pointing out what they think is unfair on the part of the managing companies. We have gone so far as to send letters, signed from 19 to 100 people and representing from 1,000,000 to 1,500,000 shares, putting forward constructive suggestions to the companies.

"No Comment"

Messrs. Wattie and Burkill had these letters for the best part of six weeks, and we then wrote them and asked if any replies would be forthcoming. One firm answered that as no questions were asked, there was nothing to which to reply. The other said they had circularized their directors and there were no comments. Well, gentlemen, if a million and a half shares does not ask for comment what are we to think?

We have tried to get Messrs. Wattie and Burkill to meet us on a round table and they won't meet us at all. This way may mean weeks and months of work, and that is possibly what we have ahead of us. We can admit we are 18 per cent. wrong, but that we are 100 per cent. wrong is ridiculous.—(Hear, Hear!)

The meeting concluded with a vote of thanks to Mr. Hickling for taking the chair, proposed by Mr. Joseph Brown.

（右侧手写批注：File / MS / 18 MAR 1936）
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年3月18日，星期三

股东保护
团体首次会议

N. W. Hickling 先生担任主席，执行委员会
当选；一名成员提出批评，要求对橡胶公司投资者进行公投

上海股东保护协会昨日下午在皇家亚洲文会大厅举行成立大会，共有44人出席，其中22人在选举执行委员会时以新组织成员身份参与投票。

N. W. Hickling 先生经投票当选为主席后，请 F. L. Morrison 先生和 L. Fearon 先生分别担任其法律顾问和秘书。

Hickling 先生说：——首先，这次会议完全是非正式的，召开此次会议的目的是为了避免将来被称为“雏形”阶段。

在着手处理诸如组建本协会和任命执行委员会等实际事务之前，我想说几句话，不仅谈谈协会的宗旨和目标，还要谈谈我们建议如何运作它。首先，我们必须量入为出；换句话说，我们可以尝试的工作在很大程度上取决于我们在银行的资金以及成员们自愿无偿付出的辛勤劳动。

我们必须按商业原则运作，这是绝对必要的，而这些原则必须基于合作俱乐部的理念，决不能抱有这种想法：一旦你支付了年度会费，你的责任——因为你没有法律责任——就完成了。Fearon 先生和我本人，以及 Pennell 先生和 Mathews 先生，在组建本协会过程中所做的工作，远超你们任何人的想象。

无固定薪金

Fearon 先生因其工作仅获得微薄的报酬。他没有固定薪水，只在必要时支取少量费用。Fearon 先生将继续担任秘书，我们的设想是，当选后的委员会将设立小组委员会，邀请成员加入并期望他们提供服务。这就是为什么我使用“合作”这个词。这些小组委员会将向执行委员会报告，执行委员会将在必要时采取行动。我真诚地相信，如果我们按这种方式运作，我们就能实现协会的目标，并成为上海一个有用且受尊重的团体。

目前我们受到怀疑，这种怀疑或许并非毫无道理。我们必须证明，虽然在这个过程中我们可能会打破一些鸡蛋，但我们始终着眼于做出煎蛋卷，并且我们具备合理的烹饪知识。

随后通过决议，正式成立名为“上海股东保护协会”的组织，并以伦敦股东保护协会的备忘录及公司章程为基础，视需要进行修改。

选举竞争

在执行委员会10名成员的选择上发生了竞争，O. Fisher 博士由现场提名。选票发给成员，要求他们写下希望剔除的人选姓名，并签名以防非成员投票。结果是 Fisher 博士被剔除，以下人员当选：W ____ 船长、T ____ 、C ____ 、Dr ____ 、L ____ 

Hickling 先生随后表示，他不打算亲自讨论协会的宗旨和目标，因为召开会议是为了完成现已完成的工作。他只是提议请任何有建议的人……

起初没有人提出问题或建议，Hickling 先生表示，他将请希望加入的非成员将姓名留给 Fearon 先生。他说，他希望召开更多会议，并能有良好的结果可以汇报。

就在会议即将结束时，Brian Bates 先生说：

公投方案

当最初提出组建该协会时，我立即寄出了一张支票，但我并不完全喜欢该协会目前的发展路线。我的想法，特别是关于橡胶公司的部分，是应该按照合并的思路来运作，而且在我看来，在对 Burkill 公司和 Watties 有限公司采取任何行动之前，应该对橡胶公司股东进行公投，看看是否能获得此类支持。当你有了背后的支持，那么你就不是请求他们做这做那，而是能够“命令”他们去做。在我看来，在我们进一步行动之前，与其对这两家公司进行琐碎的攻击，不如进行一次公投，除非你获得足够的支持，否则这表明股东们缺乏足够的兴趣。——（赞成，赞成）。

作为回应，Hickling 先生说，新一届委员会将对 Bates 先生的言论给予适当考虑。

他继续说道：——我不想告诉你们，我们只靠强力行事，即我们获得委托书和股东的支持并强行推进事务。已向你们的委员会提出了许多建议，以试图完成这项工作。你们的委员会正试图通过指出管理公司方面他们认为不公平之处来做到这一点。我们甚至已经发出了信件，由19至100人签名，代表100万至150万股股份，向各公司提出建设性建议。

“不予置评”

Wattie 和 Burkill 两家公司持有这些信件长达近六周，随后我们致函询问是否会有回复。一家公司答复称，由于未提出问题，故无可回复。另一家公司称，他们已向其董事发出通函，但没有任何评论。好吧，先生们，如果150万股股份都未能引来评论，我们该怎么想？

我们曾试图让 Wattie 和 Burkill 两家公司与我们进行圆桌会谈，但他们根本不愿与我们会面。这可能意味着数周乃至数月的工作，而这可能就是我们面前面临的局面。我们可以承认我们有18%的错误，但说我们100%错误则是荒谬的。——（赞成，赞成！）

会议最后由 Joseph Brown 先生提议，对 Hickling 先生担任主席表示感谢，会议至此结束。

（右侧手写批注：档案 / 手稿 / 1936年3月18日）
